channels.name: Zoora AI
channels.cadenceSource: CLAUDE.md, Channel 2 section: 'Zoora AI channel cadence: 2 long story episodes a week plus daily Shorts cut from them.'

pov-story.label: POV story
notes: Second person ("you"), a fictional composite protagonist, grounded in real, sourced investigations. The engine shows the fiction card (storyboard.fiction: true) for the first 5 s of the episode and of every Short.
A cautionary arc: it resolves with consequences and what the viewer can check, never a win or a lifestyle to copy (content/zoora-ai/REFERENCE.md rule 3: no income claims).
Genre only: never reuse the reference creator's character, art, scripts, thumbnails or title list, and give every episode its own structure (REFERENCE.md rules 1-2; inauthentic-content policy).
CTA: subscribe, no product pitch (the owner's pilot rule; it stays the default until the owner adds an offer).
Invented brands for any fictional token, fund, launchpad or app; real organisations only in attributed, sourced facts.

explainer.label: Explainer
notes: Zoo explains one idea with sourced facts, synthetic illustrative charts and a defensive checklist. The owner's cadence is 2 long story episodes a week, so explainers sit after the POV stories in the backlog: one appears only when pinned to a week ("week": "2026-W50") or when the stories run out.

channels.name: Zoodger News
channels.cadenceSource: CLAUDE.md, Channel 2: evergreen explainers that every news video links to; the daily news stays in scripts/daily.

reserved.label: Weekly round-up (news, made in-week)
reserved.note: The binding cadence includes a weekly long-form round-up with fund-flow analysis (CLAUDE.md, Channel 2). It is made in the week from that week's news (scripts/daily), never in the batch, so every week keeps room for it. The owner picks its day (content/zoora-security/channel.json cadence.weeklyLongForm: day TBD).

explainer.label: Evergreen explainer
notes: The talk-show set (src/show): cold open, the mechanism as a concept diagram (howItWorked), Badger's Red Flag, Zoo's One Fix, sources, and the end screen.
Concept level only: no code, function names, addresses or step lists (no exploit how-tos). Every fact attributed; no suspect or private names.
Once published, its URL goes into content/zoora-security/channel.json evergreen.<topic>.url, so the daily Threat Brief links it.

scam-of-the-week.label: Scam of the Week
notes: One recurring scam pattern as a case file (the scamOfTheWeek segment: title, how, tell, fix), built from regulators' and investigators' published descriptions, not from one victim's story.
Never at a victim's expense; never reproduce the scam's script, links, QR codes or handles.
